title: Pseudo-coherent complexes of modules are closed under direct summands
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $m$ an integer. Call a complex of $R$-modules $C^\bullet$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules and a map of complexes $E^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ inducing isomorphisms $H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C^\bullet)$ for $i>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C^\bullet)$. If $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ are complexes of $R$-modules such that $K^\bullet\oplus L^\bullet$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ are $m$-pseudo-coherent. Consequently, if $K^\bullet\oplus L^\bullet$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules, then so are $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$.

proof.text: A bounded finite free witness E -> K ⊞ L with upper bound b gives vanishing cohomology of K ⊞ L in degrees at least B=max(m,b)+1. Each homology functor sends the split epimorphisms biprod.fst and biprod.snd to epimorphisms, so both summands have vanishing cohomology there. The zero-witness lemma gives B-pseudo-coherence of both K and L.

For n >= m the original witness makes K ⊞ L n-pseudo-coherent: above n use its cohomology isomorphisms; at n=m use its epimorphism, and at n>m use its isomorphism. Transport the witness along any morphism whose homology maps are isomorphisms above n and epi at n, by composing witness maps. Apply this to the biproduct braiding to obtain the same for L ⊞ K. Suppose both K and L are (n+1)-pseudo-coherent. Apply clause one of the distinguished-triangle lemma to the split distinguished triangles K -> K ⊞ L -> L and L -> L ⊞ K -> K. This gives n-pseudo-coherence of both summands. Induct on k to obtain the simultaneous claim at degree B-k whenever m <= B-k. Taking k=(B-m).toNat proves the first clause.

Extend the existing all-m criterion from Q.obj C to any derived object using the essential surjectivity of Q and its representative isomorphism. Both pseudo-coherence and m-pseudo-coherence are invariant under this isomorphism: compose witness isomorphisms with it, or apply the generalized homology-map transport to its hom and inv. Pseudo-coherence of K ⊞ L gives m-pseudo-coherence for every m. Apply the first clause separately at each m, then the converse all-m criterion to K and L.
